title: Google signs 3.6GW deal with Constellation to secure power in PJM service area
source_used: Quartz as carried by Yahoo Finance (also Google and Constellation press release on Business Wire via Yahoo Finance; Blockspace video transcript on Yahoo Finance)
key_facts: Google and Constellation Energy announced on 6 Oct 2026 a 20-year power purchase agreement for 890 MW of new nuclear capacity on the PJM grid.
The capacity comes from upgrades (uprates) at 11 Constellation nuclear units in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey; Constellation commits more than $4.3 billion; first uprate expected by 2028.
A separate 15-year energy supply agreement covers another 2,700 MW from Constellation's existing PJM fleet (the press release says 15 years; a video transcript says 20).
Together about 3.6 GW (890 + 2,700 MW), which matches the headline figure.
Constellation also picks Google Cloud and Gemini Enterprise under an expanded five-year technology alliance.
The companies say the deal sustains about 4,400 existing jobs and creates about 7,200 construction jobs.
Amazon struck a similar 690 MW, 20-year Constellation deal at Calvert Cliffs last week.
PJM serves 67 million people (Google executive's statement).
quote_evidence: Google and Constellation Energy announced a 20-year power purchase agreement on Tuesday to bring 890 megawatts of new nuclear capacity onto the PJM Interconnection grid, with Constellation committing more than $4.3 billion to fund the build-out.

Alongside the power purchase agreement, the companies entered into a separate 15-year energy supply agreement covering an additional 2,700 megawatts from Constellation's existing fleet in the PJM market, the company said.
The first uprate is expected to be delivered by 2028.
why_it_matters_hint: Big technology companies are now paying to upgrade existing reactors and to lock up existing nuclear output for AI data centers.
